subject: Hosted API: Detailed responses to residency, retention & erasure sections
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@therabank.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: security@therabank.com
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API security questionnaire - residency & retention (Section B)

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this. Attached is Section B of our security questionnaire where we consolidate residency, retention and erasure items for the Hosted API. We have a few items we need explicit language for in our vendor review:

1) Confirmation of where customer data at rest can be stored (region/geography) for Hosted API customers.
2) Time-to-delete requirements: if a tenant requests full erasure, how long until data and backups are removed from all systems?
3) Backup & snapshot retention: do backups include persisted customer payloads and what is the maximum retention window?
4) Evidence & audit logs: can you provide a sample of an audit log entry that proves a deletion event and the retention of that audit record?
5) Any exceptions, e.g., legal holds, geo-locks, or export control constraints.

We try to get these in writing for our procurement and security teams before the end of the month. Please attach any supporting diagrams or sample log extracts.

Thanks,
Marta
Marta Lopez
Senior Vendor Risk Analyst — TheraBank
TheraBank Security Team
Attachment: TheraBank_RFI_SectionB.pdf

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@therabank.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API security questionnaire - residency & retention (Section B)

Marta —

Appreciate the clear list. Below are concise, exportable answers you can include in your vendor packet. I've attached a high-level data flow diagram for context (redwood-data-flow-diagram.png). Where you need a signed attestation or longer artifact we can follow up via our compliance portal / drive link.

1) Data residency (hosted API):
   - Primary storage location: Customers may select region(s) at provisioning time from our supported cloud regions (US West, US East, EU Central, APAC-SG depending on availability). For your account we understand the requirement is US-only; we can pin the tenant to US West (primary) and US East (replica) as needed.
   - Logical separation: Tenant data is logically partitioned; metadata and request logs are tagged with tenant IDs and region. All regional replicas remain within the selected geography.

2) Deletion/erasures (what happens on a tenant-initiated full delete):
   - Immediate effect: Application-layer rows and objects referencing customer request content are marked for deletion and excluded from future reads within seconds of the API request.
   - Physical removal: Primary datastore deletion jobs purge objects from live storage within 24–72 hours depending on in-flight requests and KV cache eviction.
   - Backups & snapshots: Any snapshot or incremental backup that contains customer payloads is queued for purge on the next maintenance cycle; typical worst-case removal from backups is 30 days from the deletion request. We offer an expedited backup purge workflow for customers with contractual SLAs (see note below).

3) Backups & snapshots:
   - Backups are incremental and encrypted at rest. They may contain de-duplicated customer payloads. Retention default: 30 days for standard hosted customers. Extended retention options available for Dedicated/Enterprise customers under contract.
   - Exemptions: Backups required for regulatory hold will be excluded from automatic purge until hold is lifted; these are rare and require documented legal process.

4) Audit evidence & logs:
   - We retain immutable audit logs for administrative actions and deletion request events for a configurable period; default retention: 365 days.
   - Sample audit extract: see attached audit-log-sample.txt — it shows timestamped deletion event, tenant identifier, triggering API key, and internal deletion job id. Audit logs are write-once within our logging pipeline and are available in our compliance bundle on request.

5) Exceptions & legal holds:
   - If a customer provides a lawful preservation request (legal hold), Redwood will suspend purge workflows for the specified objects and notify the customer of the exception. Legal holds must be documented through our support+legal intake and may require an Addendum.

Notes & operational options:
- Expedited erasure add-on: For customers requiring deletion-from-backups within 48 hours we provide a contractual add-on that triggers accelerated recovery and purge jobs (additional fee applies).
- Key management: All customer data at rest is encrypted with keys managed in our cloud KMS; we also support customer-managed keys for Enterprise customers.
- Evidence collection: We can produce a deletion attestation package (signed) for compliance reviews that includes logs, job ids, and timeline windows.

If you want, Jordan can attach a short CSV with typical backup windows and job ids and we can provide a redacted example of a deletion attestation.

Best,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Customer Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-data-flow-diagram.png

From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@therabank.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: security@therabank.com
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 13:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API security questionnaire - residency & retention (Section B)

Naomi —

Thank you, this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from Security/Legal: 

• You state "worst-case removal from backups is 30 days" — can you confirm whether that 30-day worst-case applies to both incremental and full snapshot restores?
• For the audit log sample, we need to see one that includes the internal deletion job id plus the hash of the deleted object (or a reference) so we can tie the deletion to the backup purge record.

If you can provide those two items (clarified backup window for both snapshot and incremental, and a redacted audit sample that includes the job id + object reference), we can move to Procurement. Ideally we get the sample redaction by end of day so we can include it in the risk memo.

Regards,
Marta
Attachment: none

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@therabank.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API security questionnaire - residency & retention (Section B)

Marta — Naomi looped me in for the technical details. Short answers below and I've attached two redacted artifacts for your review.

• Backup windows: both incremental (delta) backups and full snapshots are subject to the same retention policy by default. In practice: incremental backups are retained 30 days; full snapshot lifecycle is also 30 days by default unless the tenant has an extended retention contract. The reason the wording says "worst-case" is to cover the window between scheduled purge jobs and snapshot indexing — we schedule purge jobs nightly and run a final consistency pass weekly.

• Audit artifact: attached audit-log-sample.txt (redacted) contains a deletion event with: timestamp (UTC), tenant_id (redacted), api_key_hash (redacted), deletion_job_id (DJ-2026-07011-58), and object_reference (obj:r_9b5a... - truncated). The attached backup-deletion-schedule.csv maps deletion_job_id to the backup snapshot ids that were updated or marked for purge during the next maintenance cycle.

Please note these are redacted examples for procurement/security review only. If TheraBank requires full, unredacted artifacts for a deeper technical audit we can arrange a controlled review under an NDA and temporary access to our compliance drive.

Regards,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Principal Systems Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachments: backup-deletion-schedule.csv, audit-log-sample.txt
